projects.title: KIZUNA v2
projects.subtitle: Keeping a network connected when the links don’t cooperate.
projects.label: NETWORK PROTOCOL / PYTHON
projects.summary: An adaptive mesh-routing protocol with neighbor discovery, link evaluation, primary and backup paths, and a reproducible simulation environment.
projects.problem: Unstable links and disappearing nodes make routing difficult. This project explores how autonomous devices can discover neighbors, share topology and adapt their forwarding decisions when conditions change.
implementation: Protocol messages for discovery, topology sharing, routed data and emergency delivery.
Gradual neighbor admission and link-state routing with primary and backup paths.
Resilience modes and relay adaptation as links or nodes degrade.
A Docker validation environment and web simulator to make protocol behavior visible.
projects.status: Public protocol implementation with a simulation and validation setup. The web illustration on this portfolio is conceptual; it is not a live measurement of the protocol.
projects.learning: Protocol design connects algorithms with distributed behavior. The repository separates the protocol core, reproducible experiments and visual explanation so each layer can be studied independently.

projects.title: Hybrid SEC-DED Decoder
projects.subtitle: A little redundancy. A more resilient signal.
projects.label: VERILOG / ERROR CORRECTION
projects.source: Project details supplied directly by Mykhailo; source not linked publicly.
projects.summary: Extended Hamming (8,4) encoding and decoding, reliability-based correction logic, and a simulation setup comparing hard and hybrid decoding.
projects.problem: A communication channel can change a transmitted bit. This research connects the theory of error-correcting codes with an HDL implementation and an evaluation setup for comparing decoding approaches.
implementation: An extended Hamming (8,4) SEC-DED encoder and decoder in Verilog.
A custom bit layout linking syndrome values to bit positions.
Reliability checks and hybrid correction logic.
A BPSK + AWGN simulation setup for studying BER across an Eb/N0 sweep.
projects.status: Research in progress. The source has not been linked publicly, and measured BER results are not published on this page. The bit graphic is an explanatory illustration, not a benchmark.
projects.learning: The emphasis is on understanding where the decoder succeeds, where it fails and how to demonstrate correctness through testbenches and controlled experiments.

projects.title: Task Tracker
projects.subtitle: A workspace for the work behind the work.
projects.label: FULL-STACK / JAVA + REACT
projects.summary: A full-stack workspace for projects, tasks, time tracking, analytics and customizable widgets, with a Java backend and React frontend.
projects.problem: Tasks, time entries and project progress are easier to understand when they share one workspace. This application brings those workflows together behind a REST API.
implementation: JWT authentication and CRUD APIs for projects, tasks, reminders and widgets.
A React interface with a dashboard, calendar, analytics and project boards.
Active time-tracking sessions and project-progress views.
A drag-and-resize widget grid, draft/publish workflow and Docker Compose setup.
projects.status: Public source project. The repository documents backend integration tests and local startup instructions. The Generate with AI feature is a UI-only, rule-based mock; stored Java logic is not executed on the server.
projects.learning: A full-stack project brings together data modeling, authentication, API boundaries and interface state. This project also explores extensibility through configurable widgets.

projects.title: ProstaPaper
projects.subtitle: From pathology documents to a reviewable record.
projects.label: TEAM PROJECT / RAKATHON 2026
projects.source: Team project details supplied directly by Mykhailo.
projects.summary: A team hackathon prototype that proposes structured values from pathology documents and diagrams for a clinician to review before registry export.
projects.problem: Information in pathology reports and tumour diagrams needs to be converted into consistent registry fields. The challenge is to help a clinician review proposed values alongside the original documents.
implementation: A document-to-structured-record workflow for the Masaryk Memorial Cancer Institute challenge.
Source documents displayed alongside proposed extracted values.
A review step for corrections and conflicting information before confirmation.
A production architecture intended for hospital-controlled servers and local processing.
projects.status: Team hackathon prototype from RAKATHON in Brno. Individual contribution details are not yet documented here. Production deployment and live registry integration are separate validation steps. No patient data is displayed on this portfolio.
projects.learning: In document workflows, useful automation needs a clear review surface and a visible path back to the source. The interface illustration here uses generic placeholder fields.

projects.title: Study Group
projects.subtitle: A shared place to learn and get things done.
projects.label: COLLABORATION / JAVA + REACT
projects.summary: A study-group web app with chat, shared tasks, file resources, member roles and realtime notifications.
projects.problem: Study groups need a way to keep discussion, tasks and learning resources connected. The application combines them in one shared group workspace.
implementation: Group and member management with roles.
Task CRUD, deadlines and links to shared resources.
Realtime chat, typing events and online status over WebSocket.
JWT and Google OAuth2, plus documented Google Cloud deployment configuration.
projects.status: Public source project with startup and deployment instructions. This portfolio links to the code; it does not claim that a production deployment is currently online.
projects.learning: This project combines synchronous API requests with realtime events and connects authorization, file storage and collaborative interface state.

projects.title: Job Hunter Agent
projects.subtitle: Turning a noisy job feed into a useful shortlist.
projects.label: AI AUTOMATION / PYTHON
projects.summary: A Python pipeline that collects job listings, filters low-signal posts, scores relevance with Azure OpenAI and logs results to Google Sheets.
projects.problem: A job feed can contain duplicate listings, unsuitable seniority levels and unrelated posts. The pipeline applies filtering before AI-based scoring to produce a more relevant list.
implementation: Collection adapters for multiple job sources.
Prefiltering for low-signal and seniority-mismatched posts.
Azure OpenAI relevance scoring on a 0–10 scale.
Deduplication through a processed-job log and separate Google Sheets views.
projects.status: Public Python source project. Live operation depends on configured API access and source availability. Gmail reply checking is documented as disabled; no autonomous application submission is claimed here.
projects.learning: A useful AI workflow needs deterministic filtering and traceable outputs around the model. The repository separates collection, scoring and logging into distinct modules.

projects.title: Appointment System
projects.subtitle: Connecting a booking with the conversation around it.
projects.label: CLINIC APP / JAVA + TYPESCRIPT
projects.summary: A role-based clinic application for patient bookings, doctor schedules, administration and appointment-linked messaging.
projects.problem: Booking an appointment involves patients, doctor availability and staff oversight. The project models those roles and connects each appointment to its own chat thread.
implementation: Patient, doctor and admin roles with different pages and permissions.
Available-slot generation from doctor schedules and booking-conflict checks.
Appointment-linked chat over STOMP / WebSocket with a REST fallback.
Spring Security with JWT, Swagger documentation and service test files.
projects.status: Public source application with an H2 default database and PostgreSQL-ready configuration. It is presented as a software project, not a deployed clinical service.
projects.learning: The project explores role boundaries, schedule data and realtime communication while keeping booking rules on the backend.

projects.title: Video Editing Automation
projects.subtitle: From a voiceover to an editing workflow.
projects.label: CREATIVE TOOLS / PYTHON
projects.summary: A repository containing an AI-assisted editing workflow for transcription, cut planning, captions, media selection and DaVinci Resolve integration.
projects.problem: A narrated video requires many coordinated editing steps. This repository organizes them into a configurable pipeline with intermediate files and editing profiles.
implementation: Pipeline stages for transcription, cut planning and synchronized captions.
Media and audio-library indexing with style-profile configuration.
DaVinci Resolve integration scripts and an OTIO fallback path.
Storyboard, timing and timeline-validation references.
projects.status: Public repository with configurable editing stages and DaVinci Resolve integration. Full operation depends on local tools, media and configuration; the workflow has not been executed as part of creating this portfolio.
projects.learning: Creative automation benefits from visible intermediate stages so an editor can inspect and revise the result instead of treating the pipeline as a black box.
